confidence_notes: The food and drink anchors come from web searches of aggregated crowdsourced cost-of-living data and travel guides, mainly Numbeo data via Expatica (June 2026), with uHomes, Holloway, MyLifeElsewhere and Expatistan (July 2026) as cross-checks. Local prices were about AUD 25 for an inexpensive meal, AUD 123 for a mid-range meal for two, AUD 5.70 for a cappuccino, AUD 12-13 for a 0.5 L draught beer, AUD 22-25 for a cocktail and AUD 12-15 for a glass of wine. The figures differ between sources. Beer uncertainty is moderate because Melbourne serving sizes vary (pot, schooner or pint); the estimate uses a pint-sized (about 0.5 L) serving to match the cost-of-living indexes. Cocktail and wine prices are less certain than meals and coffee. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only. No booking sites were searched or checked. They assume July is winter and a softer season, and actual rates can rise sharply during major events. All USD values use the latest RBA observation (18 Nov 2026), not a July 2026 rate. This adds some currency-timing mismatch for the July pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: This is a direct estimate for Melbourne. Sydney, which costs slightly more, was used as an upper reference for drink and hotel prices, and other large Australian cities for budget accommodation.
